milops.label: Indonesia's military build-up in Papua: two new regional commands planned for 2026
milops.text: Indonesia plans two new regional military commands in 2026, one at Nabire in Central Papua and one at Sorong in Southwest Papua. About 83,000 soldiers and police are reported in the six Papuan provinces (Project Multatuli, 2026). Local groups and the TPNPB say this deepens the conflict.

milops.label: West Papua: more than 125,000 reported displaced (September 2026)
milops.text: Indonesian security forces are fighting the TPNPB in the mountainous interior of Papua. More than 125,000 people are reported displaced, though the true number is probably higher. In April 2025, an attack attributed to the TPNPB killed 15 to 17 gold miners in Yahukimo.
milops.source: Asia Pacific Report (25 Sep 2026); Wikipedia (Yahukimo massacre; TPNPB)

naval.label: AUKUS: submarine rotations at HMAS Stirling from 2027; US Naval Support Activity Stirling set up (May 2026)
naval.text: Submarine Rotational Force-West (SRF-West) brings one UK and up to four US nuclear-powered submarines to HMAS Stirling from 2027. The US Navy set up Naval Support Activity Stirling as of 30 May 2026, and US Submarine Squadron 3 is being re-established, with a lead US maintenance activity from mid-2026.
naval.source: Australian Submarine Agency; MilitarySpot (8 Jun 2026); Defence Connect (15 Jun 2026)

naval.label: Enduring US access to HMAS Stirling confirmed (August 2026)
naval.text: Australia confirmed that US attack submarines will keep enduring access to HMAS Stirling under SRF-West. This resolves uncertainty over whether the American presence would end after the first five-year period from 2027. Australia's government says it has no foreign bases, a position the arrangement is designed to keep.

naval.label: HMAS Stirling supports six Collins-class submarines and four Anzac frigates
naval.text: The naval base on Garden Island, Western Australia, supports all six Collins-class submarines and four Anzac-class frigates. The first submarine assigned permanently to Stirling was HMAS Oxley in 1987, and the Australian Submarine Squadron headquarters moved there in 1994.

naval.label: Henderson Defence Precinct and Osborne: the AUKUS shipbuilding sites (26 August 2026)
naval.text: The Henderson Defence Precinct site and boundary in Western Australia were announced on 26 August 2026. Osborne in South Australia will be the centre of construction for SSN-AUKUS nuclear-powered submarines, and HMAS Stirling will be the operating base for in-water maintenance.

naval.label: Lombrum: Australian-funded upgrade and US access; PNG says it is not a foreign base (June 2026)
naval.text: Australia funded an upgrade of the Lombrum naval base on Manus Island for the PNG Defence Force (reported at about A$500 million). Under the 2023 Defense Cooperation Agreement, the US can access the base. PNG's prime minister says Lombrum is not a foreign base.
naval.source: PINA (2 Jun 2026); Wikipedia (Lombrum Naval Base); GlobalSecurity

air.label: US B-52H bombers land at RAAF Base Tindal (1 September 2026)
air.text: B-52H Stratofortress bombers of the 2nd Bomb Wing from Barksdale Air Force Base landed at RAAF Base Tindal near Katherine on 1 September 2026, for Bomber Task Force 26-3. Tindal is also home to No. 75 Squadron's F-35A fighters and MQ-4C Triton drones.
air.source: Air & Space Forces; Army Recognition (Sep 2026); migflug (Sep 2026)

air.label: Andersen Air Force Base (Guam): America's bomber hub in the Western Pacific
air.text: Andersen Air Force Base on Guam is the current US bomber hub in the Western Pacific. Bomber Task Force deployments to Tindal are presented as a way of spreading that capacity across an allied network.

air.label: Exercise Pitch Black: the biennial RAAF exercise at Darwin and Tindal (2026 edition)
air.text: Exercise Pitch Black is a biennial warfare exercise hosted by the RAAF, normally held at RAAF Bases Darwin and Tindal. It has included forces from several partner nations, including France, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and the US. The 2026 edition is listed in August 2026 reporting.

arms.label: Tindal: the US does not say whether bombers carry nuclear weapons, and Australia does not ask
arms.text: Under the arrangement between the two governments, the US will not tell Australia whether B-52 bombers are carrying nuclear weapons when they land at RAAF Base Tindal, and the Australian government will not ask. The A$1.1bn upgrade of the base is US-funded; its scope was confirmed in October 2022.

arms.label: The Woomera Range Complex: Australia's defence test range, about 122,000 km²
arms.text: The RAAF Woomera Range Complex is the Australian Defence Force's test and evaluation range, covering about 122,000 km², with restricted airspace. It is run by the Air Warfare Centre from RAAF Base Edinburgh. Its Launch Area 5 hosted British rocket launches from 1958 to 1971.
arms.source: Wikipedia (RAAF Woomera Range Complex; Woomera Launch Area 5; RAAF Base Woomera)

arms.label: Kwajalein: the Ronald Reagan test range was renamed in 2026
arms.text: The Reagan test site on Kwajalein Atoll in the Marshall Islands, run by the US Army, was renamed the Ronald Reagan Space and Missile Test Range in 2026. It was previously the Ronald Reagan Ballistic Missile Defense Test Site (1999-2026).
arms.source: Wikipedia (Ronald Reagan Space and Missile Test Range); DVIDS (20 Apr 2026)

arms.label: OPAL reactor: 98.3% of scheduled operating time in 2025-26; no electricity generation
arms.text: ANSTO's OPAL reactor at Lucas Heights is a 20 MW research reactor using low-enriched uranium. It produces radioisotopes and neutron beams. In 2025-26 it operated 98.3% of its scheduled time. It cannot generate electricity.

arms.label: Nuclear power generation is currently illegal in Australia; uranium supplies about 8% of world demand
arms.text: Australia has a large uranium industry supplying around 8% of global demand. Nuclear power generation is currently illegal in Australia, and a nuclear power plant would take about 10 to 15 years to build.

arms.label: Napandee: the national radioactive waste facility plan was torn up after a Federal Court ruling
arms.text: The Napandee site near Kimba in South Australia was declared the site of a national radioactive waste facility. A Federal Court ruling in favour of the Barngarla traditional owners tore up the plan. Most of Australia's radioactive waste remains stored at Lucas Heights.
arms.source: ABC News (16 Jul 2024); Conservation Council SA (May 2022)

arms.label: Olympic Dam: 261,000 tonnes of contained uranium oxide; uranium is about 20% of revenue
arms.text: The Olympic Dam copper, gold and uranium mine (BHP) holds 261,000 tonnes of contained uranium oxide, and about 20% of its revenue comes from uranium. Operating uranium mines are Olympic Dam, Beverley and Four Mile in South Australia; Ranger in the Northern Territory has closed.

cyber.label: Pine Gap: protests on 20 July 2026; the government says it is a joint facility
cyber.text: Protesters gathered at Pine Gap near Alice Springs on 20 July 2026, and the facility has been the centre of a public debate about its control. Ministers say the facility is truly joint and that half its personnel are Australian. Critics say about 10% of the staff are Australian government employees; the figures differ by source.
cyber.source: The Diplomat (Jul 2026); CounterPunch (24 Jul 2026); Declassified Australia (17 Jul 2026)

cyber.label: North West Cape: a joint communications station with a significant US presence
cyber.text: The Naval Communication Station Harold E. Holt at North West Cape near Exmouth, Western Australia, is operated mainly by the Royal Australian Navy with a significant US presence, alongside the Shoal Bay and Kojarena satellite stations.
cyber.source: Operation Military Kids (2026); Wikipedia (JGGRS; Signals intelligence platforms)

cyber.label: Perth subsea cable faults (8-9 August 2026): a suspicious vessel reported
cyber.text: Two cables in the Submarine Cable Protection Zone off Perth developed faults one after the other on 8-9 August 2026, and a vessel was reportedly observed nearby. The cause has not been confirmed in this build.

geo.label: Vanuatu: the Nakamal Agreement with Australia signed on 29 June 2026
geo.text: Australia and Vanuatu signed the Nakamal Agreement in Canberra. Reported as a watered-down A$500 million security deal, it followed about ten months of negotiation after Vanuatu's prime minister pulled out of an earlier signing. In a humanitarian disaster, Vanuatu will ask Australia, New Zealand or France first.

geo.label: China-Solomon Islands security agreement (2022): visits and logistics, no declared base
geo.text: The 2022 China-Solomon Islands security agreement allows Chinese naval ship visits for logistics and stopovers. The Solomon Islands prime minister says no PLA base will be allowed. The agreement's lack of transparency has raised regional concern, especially in Australia and the US.

geo.label: Australia-PNG defence treaty: being finalised in 2025; status in 2026 not verified
geo.text: Australia and Papua New Guinea were finalising a bilateral defence treaty in 2025. Australian officials described it as the most significant upgrade to the relationship since PNG's independence in 1975. Its 2026 status was not verified in this build.
geo.source: ABC Pacific (2025); World Socialist Web Site (Sep 2025); not verified in this build

geo.label: Bougainville: independence vote ratification debated in PNG Parliament (August 2026)
geo.text: 97.7% of Bougainvilleans voted for independence in the 2019 non-binding referendum. PNG's Parliament debated whether to ratify the result in August 2026. The autonomous government says it will declare independence in 2030 if the result is not ratified.
geo.source: Asia Pacific Report (26 Aug 2026); bne IntelliNews (2026)

geo.label: New Zealand: legislated nuclear-free zone (Nuclear Free Zone, Disarmament and Arms Control Act 1987)
geo.text: New Zealand prohibits nuclear weapons and nuclear-powered vessels in its territory under a 1987 law. This is public information not verified in this build; check the current legislation.
geo.source: Public information (not verified in this build)

geo.label: Timor-Leste: an ASEAN member since 2025; Australia shares a maritime boundary treaty
geo.text: Timor-Leste joined ASEAN as its newest member. Its maritime boundary with Australia and the Greater Sunrise gas field are covered by a treaty, which was not re-verified in this build.
geo.source: IGC 2026 ASEAN background guide; not re-verified in this build

space.label: Koonibba: Australia's first Launch Facility Licence; 2026 re-entries and a DSTG mission
space.text: The Koonibba Test Range near Ceduna, South Australia, was granted Australia's first Launch Facility Licence. In 2026, Southern Launch recorded orbital re-entries W-5 and W-6, and flew a June 2026 mission for the Defence Science and Technology Group.

space.label: Rocket Lab's Māhia site: more than 80 launches; latest on 11 September 2026
space.text: Rocket Lab Launch Complex 1 on the Māhia Peninsula was the first private orbital spaceport. The last recorded launch was on 11 September 2026, and JAXA's Kakushin Rising launched from the site on 23 April 2026.

space.label: Arnhem Space Centre: the first suborbital launch; the operator moved its headquarters to Adelaide
space.text: The Arnhem Space Centre near Nhulunbuy in East Arnhem Land, operated by Equatorial Launch Australia, has hosted suborbital sounding rocket launches. The operator opened its headquarters in Adelaide rather than Darwin.

econ.label: Gorgon LNG: Stage Three expected in 2026; the largest single resource project in Australia's history
econ.text: The Chevron-operated Gorgon LNG project on Barrow Island has three LNG trains of 5.2 MTPA each and a domestic gas plant. Stage Three, with the Geryon and Eurytion fields, was expected to start production in 2026.

econ.label: Australia's LNG fleet: 10 plants and 85.1 MTPA of operating capacity (February 2026)
econ.text: As of February 2026 Australia had 10 operating LNG plants with capacity of about 85.1 MTPA. One train at North West Shelf was idle, and about 5 MTPA was under construction.

hazard.label: Cyclone Narelle (March 2026): outages at Gorgon, Wheatstone, North West Shelf and Darwin LNG
hazard.text: Tropical Cyclone Narelle, a Category 3 storm, caused outages at Gorgon and Wheatstone LNG, reduced North West Shelf output from 16.9 to 14.3 MTPA after one train shut, and took Santos's Darwin LNG offline temporarily. Ichthys reported no damage.

scs.label: Torres Strait: the PNG-Australia maritime border and the Coral Sea-Arafura Sea route
scs.text: The Torres Strait lies between Queensland and Papua New Guinea and connects the Coral Sea with the Arafura Sea. PNG determined the maritime border in the strait.

scs.label: Lombok Strait: deep enough for a submarine to transit submerged (analysis)
scs.text: Analysts describe the Lombok Strait as one of the few Indonesian passages deep enough for a submarine to transit submerged at operational depth. This is an analytical view rather than an official assessment.

wellbeing.label: World Happiness Report 2026: ranks for Australia, New Zealand and the Pacific not verified in this build
wellbeing.text: The annual report ranks countries for wellbeing. The ranks for the countries in this frame were not verified in this build; check the report directly.
wellbeing.source: World Happiness Report (annual); not verified in this build

darkweb.label: Ransomware claims for the region are group claims, not confirmed victims
darkweb.text: The Ransomware.live feed filtered to the region's country codes lists claims made by groups on their own leak sites. Each claim is labelled unverified.

markers.note: Seat of government. Australian Defence Headquarters and the Australian Signals Directorate are in the Canberra area (public information).

markers.name: Darwin (capital, Northern Territory)
markers.note: Territory capital. RAAF Base Darwin and the US Marine Rotational Force-Darwin are here (Wikipedia; Naval News, Aug 2026).

markers.note: State capital of Tasmania (public information).

markers.name: Wellington (capital, New Zealand)
markers.note: Seat of government. The New Zealand Defence Force and the GCSB are headquartered here (public information).

markers.name: Port Moresby (capital, Papua New Guinea)
markers.note: Capital; the Papua New Guinea Defence Force headquarters is here (public information).

markers.name: Honiara (capital, Solomon Islands)
markers.note: Capital. The 2022 China-Solomon Islands security agreement concerns this government (see reference items).

markers.name: Port Vila (capital, Vanuatu)
markers.note: Capital. The Nakamal Agreement with Australia was signed in Canberra on 29 June 2026 (AAP).

markers.name: Suva (capital, Fiji)
markers.note: Capital. The Republic of Fiji Military Forces headquarters is in Suva (public information).

markers.name: Nouméa (capital, New Caledonia; France)
markers.note: Capital of New Caledonia, a French territory. French armed forces are based here (public information).

markers.name: Apia (capital, Samoa)
markers.note: Capital of Samoa.

markers.name: Nuku'alofa (capital, Tonga)
markers.note: Capital of Tonga.

markers.name: Funafuti (capital, Tuvalu)
markers.note: Capital of Tuvalu, a low-lying atoll state (public information).

markers.name: Yaren (de facto capital, Nauru)
markers.note: De facto capital of Nauru, which has no formal capital.

markers.name: South Tarawa (capital, Kiribati)
markers.note: Capital of Kiribati.

markers.name: Majuro (capital, Marshall Islands)
markers.note: Capital. The Ronald Reagan test range on Kwajalein Atoll is in the same republic (see missile ranges).

markers.name: Palikir (capital, Federated States of Micronesia)
markers.note: Capital of the Federated States of Micronesia.

markers.name: Ngerulmud (capital, Palau)
markers.note: Capital of Palau, which has a Compact of Free Association with the United States.

markers.name: Hagåtña (capital, Guam; US territory)
markers.note: Capital of Guam. Andersen Air Force Base and Naval Base Guam are on the island (see foreign bases).

markers.name: Saipan (capital, Northern Mariana Islands; US)
markers.note: Capital of the Northern Mariana Islands, a US Commonwealth.

markers.name: Pago Pago (capital, American Samoa; US)
markers.note: Capital of American Samoa, a US territory.

markers.name: Avarua (capital, Cook Islands; New Zealand)
markers.note: Capital of the Cook Islands, self-governing in free association with New Zealand.

markers.name: Alofi (capital, Niue; New Zealand)
markers.note: Capital of Niue, self-governing in free association with New Zealand.

markers.name: Mata-Utu (capital, Wallis and Futuna; France)
markers.note: Capital of Wallis and Futuna, a French territory.

markers.name: Kingston (Norfolk Island; Australian territory)
markers.note: Administrative centre of Norfolk Island, an Australian external territory.

markers.name: Flying Fish Cove (Christmas Island; Australian territory)
markers.note: Settlement on Christmas Island, an Australian external territory.

markers.name: Joint Defence Facility Pine Gap (Alice Springs, NT): US-Australian signals and satellite facility
markers.note: Joint signals intelligence and satellite communications facility since 1966. About 700 military and civilian personnel (2019 count; Wikipedia). Operated by the Australian Signals Directorate with the US NSA, CIA and NRO (Wikipedia). Protests on 20 July 2026 (The Diplomat). Ministers say half the personnel are Australian; activists dispute this (Declassified Australia, Jul 2026). Position approximate.
markers.source: Wikipedia (Signals intelligence platforms; Mount Zeil); The Diplomat (Jul 2026); Declassified Australia (Jul 2026)

markers.name: Harold E. Holt Naval Communication Station (North West Cape, Exmouth, WA): US-Australian communications station
markers.note: Operated mainly by the Royal Australian Navy with a significant US presence (Operation Military Kids, 2026; Wikipedia). Position approximate.
markers.source: Operation Military Kids (2026); Wikipedia (Naval Communication Station Harold E. Holt)

markers.name: RAAF Base Darwin (Darwin, NT): US Marine Rotational Force-Darwin
markers.note: US Marines rotate through Darwin under the Marine Rotational Force-Darwin (Naval News, Aug 2026). RAAF Base Darwin and RAAF Base Tindal host Exercise Pitch Black (Wikipedia). Position approximate.

markers.name: Andersen Air Force Base (Guam): America's bomber hub in the Western Pacific
markers.note: Bomber hub in the Western Pacific (migflug, Sep 2026). Position approximate.

markers.name: Naval Base Guam (Apra Harbor, Guam) (not verified in this build)
markers.note: Public information: US Navy base on Apra Harbor. Not verified in this build.
markers.source: public information (not verified in this build)

markers.name: RAAF Base Tindal (near Katherine, NT): F-35A squadron; US B-52H bomber deployments
markers.note: B-52H bombers of the 2nd Bomb Wing (Barksdale) arrived on 1 Sep 2026 for Bomber Task Force 26-3 (Air & Space Forces; Army Recognition, Sep 2026). The A$1.1bn upgrade is US-funded (Wikipedia). No. 75 Squadron flies the F-35A; MQ-4C Triton operates here (Wikipedia). Position approximate.
markers.source: Air & Space Forces (Sep 2026); Army Recognition (Sep 2026); Wikipedia (RAAF Base Tindal)

markers.name: RAAF Base Amberley (Queensland): 82 Wing headquarters; 1 and 6 Squadrons
markers.note: Headquarters of 82 Wing; 1 and 6 Squadrons are based here (Air Combat Group, Wikipedia). US B-2 bombers deployed here in 2024 (Air & Space Forces). Position approximate.
markers.source: Wikipedia (Air Combat Group RAAF); Air & Space Forces (2024)

markers.name: RAAF Base Williamtown (NSW): F-35A 3 Squadron; 78 and 81 Wing headquarters
markers.note: Home of 3 Squadron (F-35A) and the 2 Operational Conversion Unit; 78 and 81 Wing headquarters (Air Combat Group, Wikipedia). Position approximate.

markers.name: RAAF Base Pearce (WA): 79 Squadron
markers.note: Home of 79 Squadron (Air Combat Group, Wikipedia). Position approximate.

markers.name: RAAF Base Edinburgh (Adelaide, SA): Air Warfare Centre headquarters
markers.note: Headquarters of the Air Warfare Centre; it manages the Woomera Range Complex (Wikipedia). Position approximate.

markers.name: RNZAF Base Auckland (Whenuapai, NZ) (not verified in this build)
markers.note: Public information: principal air base of the RNZAF. Position approximate; not verified in this build.
markers.source: public information (not verified in this build)

markers.name: RNZAF Base Ohakea (Manawatu, NZ) (not verified in this build)
markers.note: Public information: RNZAF base. Position approximate; not verified in this build.
markers.source: public information (not verified in this build)

markers.name: HMAS Stirling (Garden Island, WA): Fleet Base West and submarine base for AUKUS rotations
markers.note: Home of the six Collins-class submarines and of the Anzac-class frigates. Submarine Rotational Force-West (one UK and up to four US nuclear-powered submarines) from 2027. US Naval Support Activity Stirling was established on 30 May 2026; enduring US access was confirmed in August 2026 (ASA; Defence Connect, Jun 2026; Army Recognition, Aug 2026). Position approximate.
markers.source: Australian Submarine Agency (SRF-West); Defence Connect (15 Jun 2026); MilitarySpot (8 Jun 2026); Army Recognition (9 Aug 2026)

markers.name: Fleet Base East (Garden Island, Sydney): Royal Australian Navy east-coast base
markers.note: East-coast fleet base in Sydney (Royal Australian Navy material, via a secondary summary; the position was not independently verified in this build).
markers.source: Royal Australian Navy (via secondary summary); partly verified in this build

markers.name: HMAS Coonawarra (Darwin, NT): Royal Australian Navy northern base (not verified in this build)
markers.note: Public information: Royal Australian Navy base in Darwin. Not verified in this build.
markers.source: public information (not verified in this build)

markers.name: Lombrum Naval Base (Manus Island, PNG): PNG Defence Force base with Australian-funded upgrade and US access
markers.note: Australian-funded upgrade (about A$500 million; PINA, Jun 2026). US access under the 2023 Defense Cooperation Agreement. PNG's prime minister says it is not a foreign base (PINA, 2 Jun 2026). Built by the US in 1944 (GlobalSecurity).
markers.source: PINA (2 Jun 2026); GlobalSecurity (Lombrum); Wikipedia (Lombrum Naval Base)

markers.name: HMNZS Devonport (Auckland, NZ): Royal New Zealand Navy base (not verified in this build)
markers.note: Public information: Royal New Zealand Navy base. Not verified in this build.
markers.source: public information (not verified in this build)

markers.name: French Armed Forces in New Caledonia (FANC), Nouméa (not verified in this build)
markers.note: Public information: French forces in New Caledonia. Not verified in this build.
markers.source: public information (not verified in this build)

markers.name: RAAF Woomera Range Complex (SA): Australian Defence Force test and evaluation range (about 122,000 km²)
markers.note: Test and evaluation range run by the RAAF for defence materiel; the Woomera Prohibited Area and its restricted airspace are controlled by the RAAF. Launch Area 5 hosted British rocket launches from 1958 to 1971 (Wikipedia). Coordinates are for Launch Area 5.
markers.source: Wikipedia (RAAF Woomera Range Complex; Woomera Launch Area 5)

markers.name: Ronald Reagan Space and Missile Test Range (Kwajalein Atoll, Marshall Islands): US Army test range
markers.note: Renamed in 2026 from the Ronald Reagan Ballistic Missile Defense Test Site; run by the US Army Kwajalein Atoll (Wikipedia; DVIDS, Apr 2026). Minuteman III test launches from Vandenberg have flown to this range (Newsweek, navigational warnings, 2025).
markers.source: Wikipedia (Ronald Reagan Space and Missile Test Range); DVIDS (Apr 2026); Newsweek (2025)

markers.name: Koonibba Test Range (SA; Southern Launch): sub-orbital and re-entry test range
markers.note: Australia's first Launch Facility Licence (SpaceAustralia, 2021). The range covers up to 41,000 km². 2026 orbital re-entries W-5 and W-6, and a June 2026 mission for Defence Science and Technology Group (AeroVia, 2026). Position approximate.

markers.name: Arnhem Space Centre (Nhulunbuy, NT): commercial spaceport (Equatorial Launch Australia)
markers.note: Operated by Equatorial Launch Australia. The first suborbital sounding rocket was launched from here; the operator's headquarters moved to Adelaide (Wikipedia, 2026). Position approximate.

markers.name: Rocket Lab Launch Complex 1 (Māhia Peninsula, NZ): private orbital spaceport
markers.note: The world's first private orbital spaceport; more than 80 launches. The last launch was on 11 Sep 2026 (rocketlaunch.org, 2026). Kakushin Rising (JAXA) launched from here on 23 Apr 2026 (Rocket Lab).

markers.name: Abbot Point spaceport (Queensland) (listed in 2026 launch sites; not verified in this build)
markers.note: Listed among 2026 orbital launch sites (Gunter's Space Page). Not verified in this build; position approximate.
markers.source: Gunter's Space Page (2026 listing); not verified in this build

markers.name: Canberra Deep Space Communication Complex (Tidbinbilla, ACT): NASA deep-space station (not verified in this build)
markers.note: Public information: NASA's Australian deep-space tracking station. Not verified in this build.
markers.source: public information (not verified in this build)

markers.name: Defence Receiving Station Shoal Bay (Darwin, NT): Australian Signals Directorate satellite and HF intercept
markers.note: Controlled by the Australian Signals Directorate; satellite communications interception and HF signals (Wikipedia, Signals intelligence platforms by nation).
markers.source: Wikipedia (Signals intelligence operational platforms by nation)

markers.name: Australian Defence Satellite Communications Station (Kojarena, WA): satellite communications
markers.note: Part of the Defence satellite communications network near Kojarena (Wikipedia, Joint Geological and Geophysical Research Station). Position approximate.
markers.source: Wikipedia (Joint Geological and Geophysical Research Station)

markers.name: Joint Geological and Geophysical Research Station (Alice Springs, NT): seismic monitoring, US and Australian
markers.note: Seismic monitoring station (USAF and Australian Defence). Its data are processed in Canberra and shared with seismologists and international agencies (Wikipedia). Position approximate.
markers.source: Wikipedia (Joint Geological and Geophysical Research Station)

markers.name: Australian Signals Directorate headquarters (Canberra) (not verified in this build)
markers.note: Public information: Australia's signals and cyber agency. Position approximate; not verified in this build.
markers.source: public information (not verified in this build)

markers.name: GCSB headquarters (Wellington, NZ) (not verified in this build)
markers.note: Public information: New Zealand's signals and cyber agency. Position approximate; not verified in this build.
markers.source: public information (not verified in this build)

markers.name: Waihopai signals station (Blenheim, NZ): historic intercept station; current status not verified in this build
markers.note: Historic GCSB satellite intercept station. Its current status was not verified in this build. Position approximate.
markers.source: public information (not verified in this build)

markers.name: Australian Defence Headquarters (Russell, Canberra) (not verified in this build)
markers.note: Public information: Australia's defence headquarters. Position approximate; not verified in this build.
markers.source: public information (not verified in this build)

markers.name: New Zealand Defence Force headquarters (Wellington) (not verified in this build)
markers.note: Public information: NZDF headquarters. Position approximate; not verified in this build.
markers.source: public information (not verified in this build)

markers.note: Public information: the RFMF headquarters. Position approximate; not verified in this build.
markers.source: public information (not verified in this build)

markers.name: OPAL multi-purpose research reactor (Lucas Heights, Sydney): ANSTO's 20 MW research reactor
markers.note: Australia's only nuclear reactor: a 20 MW research reactor using low-enriched uranium. It operated 98.3% of its scheduled time in 2025-26 (ANSTO). It produces radioisotopes and neutron beams and cannot produce electricity (ANSTO; Nuclear Engineering International).

markers.name: HIFAR research reactor (Lucas Heights; 1958-2007): decommissioning under way
markers.note: Australia's first research reactor, operated 1958-2007 and now being decommissioned. Radiological waste is managed on site (ANSTO, 2026).

markers.name: Lucas Heights waste stores (ANSTO): legacy and intermediate-level radioactive waste storage
markers.note: Most of Australia's radioactive waste is stored at Lucas Heights; the former MOATA reactor remains encased in concrete and steel (ABC News, Jul 2024; Conservation Council SA, 2022).
markers.source: ABC News (16 Jul 2024); Conservation Council SA (2022)

markers.name: Napandee (near Kimba, SA): proposed National Radioactive Waste Management Facility (plan halted by court ruling)
markers.note: The 2020-21 site declaration was torn up after a Federal Court ruling in favour of the Barngarla traditional owners (ABC News, Jul 2024). Position approximate.
markers.source: ABC News (16 Jul 2024); Conservation Council SA (May 2022)

markers.name: Olympic Dam mine (Roxby Downs, SA): copper, gold and uranium (BHP)
markers.note: Underground mine with 261,000 tonnes of contained uranium oxide; about 20% of revenue comes from uranium (World Nuclear Association).

markers.name: Beverley uranium mine (SA; in-situ recovery) (approximate position)
markers.note: Operating uranium mine using in-situ recovery (World Nuclear Association). Position approximate.

markers.name: Four Mile uranium mine (SA; in-situ recovery) (approximate position)
markers.note: Operating uranium mine using in-situ recovery (World Nuclear Association). Position approximate.

markers.name: Ranger uranium mine (Jabiru, NT): closed; rehabilitation under the closure plan
markers.note: Closed. Rehabilitation is planned over about seven years under the 2020 closure plan (World Nuclear Association).

markers.name: Maralinga and Emu Field (SA): British nuclear weapons test sites, 1956-1963 (not verified in this build)
markers.note: Public information: British atomic tests in the 1950s and 1960s; clean-up disputes continue. Not verified in this build.
markers.source: public information (not verified in this build)

markers.name: Monte Bello Islands (WA): British atomic test site, 1952-1957 (not verified in this build)
markers.note: Public information: the first British atomic test (1952) was held here. Not verified in this build.
markers.source: public information (not verified in this build)

markers.name: Henderson Defence Precinct (Western Australia): AUKUS submarine and shipbuilding precinct
markers.note: Site and boundary announced on 26 Aug 2026. It supports the sustainment pipeline for the submarine programme, about 10,000 jobs over two decades (Australian Submarine Agency, 26 Aug 2026).

markers.name: Osborne shipyard (Adelaide, SA): construction centre for SSN-AUKUS submarines
markers.note: Will be the centre of construction for Australia's SSN-AUKUS nuclear-powered submarines (Australian Submarine Agency, 26 Aug 2026).

markers.name: Torres Strait (Australia-PNG): sea route between the Coral Sea and the Arafura Sea
markers.note: Between Queensland and Papua New Guinea. PNG determined the maritime border in the strait (Wikipedia). It connects the Coral Sea and the Arafura Sea (Anantam IAS, 2026). Position approximate.

markers.name: Bass Strait (Victoria-Tasmania): between mainland Australia and Tasmania
markers.note: Connects the Tasman Sea and the Southern Ocean; separates mainland Australia from Tasmania (Anantam IAS, 2026). Position approximate.

markers.name: Cook Strait (New Zealand): between the North and South Islands (not verified in this build)
markers.note: Public information: the strait that carries New Zealand's main undersea and ferry links between the islands. Not verified in this build.
markers.source: public information (not verified in this build)

markers.name: Vitiaz Strait (Papua New Guinea): between New Guinea and New Britain (not verified in this build)
markers.note: Public information: a PNG strait on a major sea route north of the Solomon Sea. Not verified in this build.
markers.source: public information (not verified in this build)

markers.name: Gorgon LNG (Barrow Island, WA): 15.6 MTPA, three trains; domestic gas plant (300 TJ/d)
markers.note: Chevron-operated. Three LNG trains of 5.2 MTPA each; the first cargo left in March 2016; a 90 km domestic pipeline links the island to the mainland (Chevron; Wikipedia). Stage Three (Geryon and Eurytion fields) was expected to start production in 2026 (Offshore Technology). Position approximate.
markers.source: Chevron (fact sheet); Offshore Technology; Wikipedia (Gorgon gas project)

markers.name: North West Shelf LNG (Karratha, WA): 14.3 MTPA; one of five trains shut (Woodside, 2026)
markers.note: Australia's oldest LNG project. One of five production trains was shut after the March 2026 cyclone (Hydrocarbon Processing, Mar 2026). Position approximate.

markers.name: Pluto LNG (Karratha, WA; Woodside) (approximate position)
markers.note: Downtime at Pluto in 2026 lowered Woodside's production guidance (Hydrocarbon Processing, Mar 2026). Position approximate.

markers.name: Wheatstone LNG (Onslow, WA; Chevron) (approximate position)
markers.note: Outages in March 2026 were likely due to Tropical Cyclone Narelle (Hydrocarbon Processing, Mar 2026). Position approximate.

markers.name: Ichthys LNG (offshore field off WA; onshore plant near Darwin, NT; Inpex)
markers.note: Two trains of 4.0 MTPA each, commissioned in 2018 (SEALA AI, 2026). Inpex reported no damage from the 2026 cyclone (Hydrocarbon Processing, Mar 2026). Position approximate.

markers.name: Darwin LNG (Wickham Point, NT; Santos): 3.7 MTPA; temporarily offline after the March 2026 cyclone
markers.note: A 3.7 MTPA plant that was offline temporarily after the March 2026 cyclone (Hydrocarbon Processing, Mar 2026). Position approximate.

markers.name: Curtis Island LNG (Gladstone, Queensland): Queensland Curtis, Australia Pacific and Gladstone LNG
markers.note: Coal-seam gas export plants on Curtis Island; part of Australia's ten-plant LNG fleet with 85.1 MTPA of capacity (SEALA AI, Feb 2026). Position approximate.

markers.name: Dampier to Bunbury Natural Gas Pipeline (Western Australia): main gas trunk line
markers.note: The domestic gas trunk line that the Gorgon domestic pipeline ties into (Offshore Technology; Chevron). Position approximate (route midpoint).

markers.name: PNG LNG (Hides, Southern Highlands, PNG): gas conditioning plant and over 450 km of onshore pipeline
markers.note: Hides gas field and gas conditioning plant, with over 450 km of onshore pipeline (Spiecapag, 2026). Position approximate.

markers.name: Tangguh LNG (Bintuni Bay, West Papua, Indonesia): LNG expansion (approximate position)
markers.note: Expansion project on the southern shore of Bintuni Bay (Spiecapag, 2026). Position approximate.

markers.name: Moomba gas field and plant (SA) and gas pipeline to Sydney (not verified in this build)
markers.note: Public information: the Moomba-Sydney gas pipeline. Not verified in this build; position approximate.
markers.source: public information (not verified in this build)

markers.name: Submarine cable protection zone off Perth: two cable faults on 8-9 August 2026 (reported)
markers.note: Two cables faulted one after the other on 8-9 August 2026; a vessel was reportedly seen nearby (SpecialEurasia, 11 Aug 2026). Reported; not confirmed in this build.

markers.name: West Papua highlands (Puncak, Yahukimo): TPNPB insurgency; more than 125,000 reported displaced
markers.note: Indonesian security forces are fighting the West Papua National Liberation Army (TPNPB). More than 125,000 people are reported displaced (Asia Pacific Report, 25 Sep 2026). The April 2025 Yahukimo attack killed 15 to 17 gold miners (Wikipedia; AP). Position approximate.
markers.source: Asia Pacific Report (25 Sep 2026); Wikipedia (Yahukimo massacre); AP (2025)

markers.name: Bougainville (Buka and Arawa): independence vote; PNG Parliament ratification pending
markers.note: 97.7% of voters chose independence in the 2019 non-binding referendum. PNG Parliament debated ratification in August 2026; the autonomous government plans to declare independence in 2030 (Asia Pacific Report, 26 Aug 2026). Position approximate.
markers.source: Asia Pacific Report (26 Aug 2026); bne IntelliNews (2026)

markers.name: Jakarta (capital, Indonesia)
markers.note: Capital of Indonesia.

markers.name: Dili (capital, Timor-Leste)
markers.note: Capital of Timor-Leste (East Timor).

markers.name: Surabaya (East Java): Indonesian Navy 2nd Fleet and submarine base
markers.note: Home port of the Type 209 boats KRI Nagapasa, KRI Ardadedali and KRI Alugoro; the 2nd Fleet Command is based here (Wikipedia). Position approximate.

markers.name: PT PAL Indonesia shipyard (Surabaya): builds two Scorpene Evolved submarines
markers.note: State shipbuilder. First steel was cut on 7 Aug 2026 for the lead Scorpene Evolved boat; the Navy expects delivery in 2032-33 (Antara; Navy Leaders). Naval Group provides design support. Position approximate.

markers.name: Halim Perdanakusuma Air Force Base (Jakarta): National Air Operations Command
markers.note: National Air Operations Command (Koopsudnas) is headquartered here. The base hosts transport and VIP squadrons; the civil airport shares the runway (Global Military, Aug 2026; Wikipedia).
markers.source: Global Military (Aug 2026); Wikipedia (Halim Perdanakusuma International Airport)

markers.name: Iswahjudi Air Force Base (Maospati, East Java): fighter base, 32nd Air Wing
markers.note: Home to the 32nd Air Wing and four other units (ICAO WARI; Global Military, Aug 2026).

markers.name: Sultan Hasanuddin Air Force Base (Makassar): 33rd Air Wing, Su-27/Su-30
markers.note: Su-30MK2 overran the runway on 24 Aug 2026 during a simulated take-off after a major overhaul; the crew was unhurt (migflug, 2026). Position approximate.

markers.name: Manuhua Air Force Base (Biak, Papua): 13th Air Wing; 27th Air Squadron (CN235)
markers.note: ICAO WABB; runway 11/29, 3,571 m (migflug, 2026; Wikipedia). Position approximate.

markers.name: Raden Sadjad Air Force Base (Ranai, Natuna Islands)
markers.note: ICAO WIDO; runway 18/36, 2,560 m (Wikipedia, Indonesian Air Force listing). The Natuna Islands face the South China Sea. Position approximate.

markers.name: Sunda Strait (Java-Sumatra)
markers.note: Strait between Java and Sumatra (public information). Not verified in this build.
markers.source: public information (not verified in this build)

markers.name: Lombok Strait (Bali-Lombok)
markers.note: Deep-water route between the Java Sea and the Indian Ocean (public information). Not verified in this build.
markers.source: public information (not verified in this build)

markers.name: Makassar Strait (Borneo-Sulawesi)
markers.note: Strait between Borneo and Sulawesi (public information). Not verified in this build.
markers.source: public information (not verified in this build)
